prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The Liberal Democrats set out a liberal, internationalist plan to build and safeguard a fair, free and open society—balancing liberty, equality and community—so everyone can thrive and no one is held back by poverty, ignorance or conformity.

Stop Brexit to build a brighter future: Revoke Article 50 with a Lib Dem majority; otherwise back a People’s Vote. Protect freedom of movement, UK-EU citizens’ rights and Gibraltar. Use a £50bn Remain Bonus to invest in schools and tackling inequality.

A stronger, fairer economy: Invest £130bn in infrastructure (transport, energy, schools, hospitals, homes) and a £50bn Regional Rebalancing Programme plus a Just Transition Fund. Introduce a wellbeing budget. Raise R&D to 3% of GDP, expand Catapults, and back green innovation. Support SMEs and startups, prompt payment, local banking, and town centre renewal.

Responsible capitalism and fair taxes: Employee voice on boards, due diligence for environment and human rights, shareholder binding votes on pay. Restore corporation tax to 20%, replace business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy, tax income from wealth more like work, and clamp down on multinational tax avoidance.

Skills and the future of work: A £10,000 Skills Wallet for every adult; expand high-quality apprenticeships and National Colleges. New rights for gig-economy workers, flexible working from day one, stronger enforcement, and a genuine Living Wage across sectors.

Education and childcare: Free, high-quality childcare from nine months for working parents (35 hours, 48 weeks). Reverse school cuts, hire 20,000 teachers, fix buildings, boost SEND. Scrap SATs and Ofsted, replace with broader assessment and a new inspectorate. Restore FE funding, maintenance grants, student mental health standards; protect arts and sport.

Climate and nature first: Net zero by 2045; at least 80% renewable electricity by 2030; ban fracking. A 10‑year home insulation and zero‑carbon heat programme to end fuel poverty by 2025. All new cars electric by 2030; rail network ultra‑low‑emission by 2035; invest in buses, trams, walking and cycling. A Nature Act with binding targets, 60m trees a year, major habitat restoration, a circular economy and tougher waste and plastics rules. Strong animal welfare reforms.

Health and social care: Raise £7bn/year via 1p on Income Tax (ringfenced), £10bn capital, and develop a dedicated Health & Care Tax. Integrate NHS, social care and public health. Parity for mental health: new waiting-time standards, 24/7 crisis care, perinatal support, student charter, gambling reforms.

A fair society: Make Universal Credit supportive—first payment in 5 days, end the two‑child limit, bedroom tax, punitive sanctions; raise Local Housing Allowance; legal right to food. Build 300,000 homes a year including 100,000 for social rent; Rent to Own; private renting reform; end rough sleeping in five years.

Safety and justice: Restore community policing (£1bn), adopt a public‑health approach to violence, invest in youth services, create an Online Crime Agency, end disproportionate Stop & Search. Make prisons rehabilitative, presume against short sentences, expand restorative justice, reduce BAME disparities.

Rights, equality, migration: Defend the Human Rights Act and ECHR; curb mass surveillance and police facial recognition. Strengthen equality law (GRA reform, ‘X’ passports, BSL Act, end period poverty). Scrap the hostile environment; end indefinite detention (28‑day limit); flexible work and study visas; right to work for asylum seekers after 3 months; resettle vulnerable refugees, including 10,000 unaccompanied children over 10 years.

Better politics and devolved power: Proportional representation (STV), votes at 16, votes for long‑term EU residents and UK citizens abroad; reform the Lords; tougher transparency and media standards; citizens’ assemblies. A federal UK with real powers for nations, regions and communities.

A better world: Lead through the EU, UN, NATO and WTO; uphold 0.7% aid; global climate action; Magnitsky sanctions; suspend arms sales to Saudi Arabia; recognise Palestine; support Ukraine and Hong Kong; meet NATO 2% and strengthen cyber defence while maintaining a minimum nuclear deterrent alongside multilateral disarmament efforts.
